issues.evidence: Customer email (received 2026-10-14): 'The van driver, Mr. Dubois, admitted it was his fault and we both signed the accident report' — the third party is named (Mr. Dubois) and both drivers signed the accident report, so the third party is identified. Veridia contract Article 5.2 (contract.pdf, 2630#10414, p.2): for C2, no deductible at all applies when the authorised driver is not at fault AND the third party is identified. Because the handler recorded 'identified: false', the system applied the €300 standard C2 deductible (payout €900); with the third party identified as the email states, the not-at-fault waiver applies and the deductible should be €0 (payout €1,200).

verdict.summary: All other facts check out (C2 in the Policy Schedule, incident 2026-10-12, reported 2026-10-14 within the 5-day deadline of Article 4.1, €1,200 quote matching the email, policyholder not at fault, all three C2 documents received, no exclusion, no assessor needed since €1,200 is not above €1,500 per Article 6.1, and the van being a commercial vehicle is handled by the pending_approval referral per the playbook), but the third party is named in the email (Mr. Dubois, signed accident report) so 'identified: false' is wrong and the €300 deductible should be waived under Article 5.2.
